title: Egyptian state founded: first cities (Thinis, Nekheb) — Menes/Mizraim
summary: CFAH AP-3: the Egyptian state was founded with its first cities 2189/2188 BC; CFAH identifies Menes with Mizraim son of Ham.
description: CFAH-6 (section "Argument 1") identifies "the biblical Mizraim as Menes, the founder of Egypt shortly after the Biblical Dispersion (Genesis 10:13–14; 50:11)". CFAH-2 Conclusions date the founding of Thinis to 2188 BC. Ussher (Second Age §51) independently places Mizraim's colony in Egypt in 2188 BC.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 2: Founding of the Nations," ARJ 15 (2022): 405–426, section "Founding of the Nations", Table 3 (AP-3 "Egyptian Cities Founded", 2189/2188; Diodorus, Manetho, Cullimore, Constantinus Manassas, Varro); also CFAH-6 Argument 2, Table 1 "Anchor Points for early Egyptian history" #3
chronologies.note: CFAH-6 Table 1: "Egyptian state was founded with the first cities, Thinis, Nekheb, etc."

chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Second Age §51 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
chronologies.note: "About this time Mizraim, the son of Ham, led his colony into Egypt" (Constantinus Manasses: the Egyptian state lasted 1663 years, counted back from Cambyses). Agrees with CFAH AP-3 (2188 BC).
Jones (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament, 2002) gives no date for this extra-biblical event.

chronologies.citation: Taking Africa for Jesus, ch. 2 "Egypt (Part 1)", PDF p. 19 (printed p. 19)
chronologies.note: Mizraim possibly began to settle Egypt about this time. Differs from the sort year (2189 BC, cfah-anchor) by 261 years.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 7 "The Return of the Nephilim: Nimrod Attempts World Empire", PDF p. 157 (printed p. 143)
chronologies.note: Monarchy of Mizraim (Menes) begins in Egypt at the Dispersion. Differs from the sort year (2189 BC, cfah-anchor) by 2 years.

chronologies.date: “The priests said that Min was the first king of Egypt”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.99 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 135 (PDF p. 137)
chronologies.note: Min dammed the Nile and founded Memphis (2.99). Identification agrees: CFAH identifies the first king, Menes, with Mizraim (CFAH-2 AP-3, 2189/2188 BC).

chronologies.date: “the names of three hundred and thirty monarchs, who (they said) were his successors upon the throne”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.100 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 135 (PDF p. 137)
chronologies.note: Read to Herodotus from a papyrus: 18 Ethiopian kings and one native queen among them. CONFLICT in structure: Herodotus has a single succession of 330 reigns from Min to Moeris, where CFAH treats the Egyptian dynasties as parallel (CFAH-6), with only about 510 years between Menes (2189 BC) and Moeris (about 1679 BC).

chronologies.date: “Thus the whole number of years is eleven thousand, three hundred and forty”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.142 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 157 (PDF p. 159)
chronologies.note: 341 generations of kings and high priests from the first king (Min) to Sethos, at three generations to a century; within it the sun four times "moved from his wonted course". DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): Sethos at the time of Sennacherib (Generations, about 713 BC, provisional) + 11,340 = about 12,050 BC for Min. CONFLICT with the framework and CFAH: CFAH dates Menes 2189/2188 BC (AP-3) and Creation 4004 BC (AP-30). The 11,340 years exceed the whole span from Creation to Herodotus.
